analysis: Pseudotumour cerebri, or idiopathic intracranial hypertension, is a condition where there is increased intracranial pressure without a detectable cause. Certain medications are known to be associated with this condition, and tetracycline is one of the most well-documented drugs in this regard. The mechanism is not entirely understood, but it is believed that tetracycline can lead to increased intracranial pressure, possibly due to its effects on cerebrospinal fluid dynamics. The other options, sparfloxacin, gentamicin, and clofazimine, do not have a recognized association with Pseudotumour cerebri in the medical literature. Therefore, based on standard medical knowledge and consensus, tetracycline is the most likely drug to cause Pseudotumour cerebri.
